newsitem.title: GERMANY: German equities fall in lacklustre early trade.
newsitem.headline: German equities fall in lacklustre early trade.

text.p: German shares fell around one percent in early bourse dealings on Friday, tracking losses from electronic trade on Thursday, with low volumes and high volatility characterising trade on the blue-chip DAX index.
The DAX index was down 43.15 points, or 1.02 percent, at 4,188.28 points, while the September DAX future contract was up three points at 4,196 points.

"We are expecting a manipulated market today. There is a small options expiry which will probably come in around 4,200 points, and because of holidays in many parts of Europe volumes will be very low," a trader said.
There was little market moving data around to help the DAX make a significant move in any direction, either towards a meaningful correction or a new rally.

Dealers said that focused continued on utility RWE AG, which on Wednesday night announced plans to shelve an unpopular system of multiple voting rights attached to shares held mainly by local municipalities.
The move was viewed as opening up the company to international investors, by loosening old ties on its equity.
Holders of preferred shares in RWE will be invited to swap these for common shares under the new voting rights system.
RWE common stock was up 90 pfennigs at 87.90 marks in early bourse, not quite equalling the dizzy heights of Thursday.
The Assumption holiday in the southern states of Germany also contributed to lacklustre share trade.
